GROUP EMPLOYEE OPD BENEFITS PLAN BOOKLET

OPD Guidelines 
• The period will be from 1st July 2025 to 30th June 2026 and shall be 
renewed for this period in subsequent years. 
• Only employees, their spouses and children are eligible. Only 3 
children will be eligible for coverage. 
• Claims will be sent and processed batch -wise on a monthly basis. 
They will be sent on the 1st of every month. 
• Claim validity will be a maximum of 60 days from incurrence to the 
dispatching date. Claims older than 60 days will not be entertained. 
• All claims will require a copy of prescriptions, original bills and 
original receipts. 
• In the case of chronic disease medications (e.g. arthritis, 
hypertension, diabetes, etc.), only prescriptions of up to 6 months 
will be entertained. Fresh prescriptions will be required if previous 
prescriptions are older than 6 months from date of issuance.

I. INTRODUCTION 
BCER companies based in Europe, the Middle East and Africa ("BCER" or the
"Company") shall take appropriate and reasonable measures to safeguard and 
secure electronic networks, equipment, and information contained thereon, against 
unauthorized access, modification, theft or usage. 
II. APPLICABILITY 
1
. The BCER EMEA Information Asset Protection Policy (the "Policy") is applicable to
all employees of the Company, and independent contractors and consultants using
electronic equipment or networks to conduct BCER business, regardless of whether
such equipment or networks are owned by BCER, or connected to BCER systems.
2. This Policy is applicable to all BCER lines of business and departments in the EMEA
region, including all corporate office locations, shared service and operational
business units. It applies to independently operated subsidiaries such as BCER
Global Investors and Trammel Crow Company. The Policy represents the minimum
standards for IT Disaster Recovery within BCER.
3. In the event of any conflict between the requirements of this Policy and local law or
policy, local law or policy shall control, but only with regard to those sections which
give rise to conflict; all other sections of this Policy shall remain in force and
applicable.
III. DEFINITIONS 
A
. "Application" means any software or hardware, including end-user developed 
applications utilising software such as Excel, Access or Cloud Providers such as 
Amazon Web Services, designed to perform a specific function directly for the user 
or, in some cases, for another application program and that BCER utilizes in the
course of business operations. 
B. "Business Application Owner" means an individual within a business team (as 
opposed to the local or EMEA or Global IT function or the Business Continuity 
Office) that is assigned ownership of an Application or Applications used by the 
business team that will serve as a point of contact for local or EMEA or Global IT 
and the Business Continuity Office and will fulfill certain responsibilities within 
this Policy. 
C.

C. "Confidential Information" means Information Assets which because of their 
sensitive nature should be treated confidentially due to the risk that unauthorized 
use, disclosure, destruction or modification could cause financial, reputational or 
other harm to the Company, employees, vendors or clients, or subject the 
Company to civil, criminal, regulatory or other legal sanctions. Confidential 
Information includes but is not limited to: 
1. Personnel, medical, salary, performance or other employee records;
2. Financial records, trade secrets, information subject to a confidentiality
agreement;

3. Information deemed private or confidential by law, including but not
limited to personally identifiable financial information, personal medical
records, and the like;
4. Information deemed private or confidential by BCER or Company
vendors or clients; and
5. Information which in the normal course of business is reasonably
expected to remain confidential by BCER employees, clients, vendors,
regulatory bodies, and others.
D. "Device" includes desktop computers, laptops, notebooks, hard or flash storage 
drives (or any other similar device), smartphones (including but not limited to 
Apple, Android, Blackberry, and Windows phones) or any other similar tablet, 
slate, PDA, phone or media device used to access Company Networks or 
Information Assets. 
1. "Mobile Device" Incudes all of the above excluding desktop
computers but includes whether personally owned or owned by
BCER.
E. "Information Assets" includes: 
1. Data, documents, data compilations, software or hardware stored, filed,
created, documented and/or maintained, on or in connection with the
Company's central computer network or systems; and
2. Any Device (whether owned by BCER or not) with access to or operating
on BCER Networks.
F. "IT" means BCER's Information Technology Department (local, EMEA or 
Global). 
G. "IT Disaster Recovery" means the technology strategies and plans used to restore 
Information Assets to meet business and regulatory requirements following a 
disruption. 
H. "Networks" means BCER's computer network or systems including but not 
limited to the Mainframe, LAN and WAN. 
IV. POLICY
A. Global IT Activated Security Requirements 
1. Certification
a. Individuals who use BCER Networks or any Device for
transacting BCER business must certify annually that they have
reviewed and are in compliance with this Policy.
2. Passwords
a. The Company shall establish and maintain individual access
identification and confirmation security protocols for all 
relevant Networks and Devices that provide access to 
Information Assets. These protocols shall include but not be

limited to the following minimum standards: 
i. Each individual accessing BCER Networks must be
assigned an individual access identification
("Password").
ii. Security protocols must include Password expiration
within a reasonable period, to be no more than sixty 
(60) days or upon termination of an employee or 
other person with access to Company Networks. 
iii. Password security protocols shall be reviewed and
assessed periodically to conform to regulatory
changes or industry norms related to applicable
Networks or Devices.
b. Password Assignments and Approvals.
i. The supervisor of an employee requiring access to
Company Networks must approve and submit the
proper user request form to a local or EMEA IT or HR
representative. The local or EMEA IT Helpdesk will
then provide the employee with access to the relevant
Networks.
ii. Access by clients and/or other third parties must be
approved by the appropriate Head of Department
following the same procedures in the paragraph
above.
c. Password Deemed Confidential.
i. BCER deems Company required passwords to be
Confidential Information. Employees are prohibited
from sharing a Password with any other person unless
prior written authorization is obtained by the
applicable Head of Department.
ii. Written authorization will only be granted in the rare
circumstances when conditions prevent delegated
access being provided.
d. Password Deactivation; Security Lockdown
i. When an employee or other person no longer requires
access to Company Networks (e.g., leaves the
Company, leave-of-absence, etc.), the appropriate line
manager or Department Head shall notify the HR
department as soon as possible after receipt of notice
of such person no longer requiring access so that
arrangements can be made to revoke access privileges
on the appropriate date.
ii. For persons described in 2.d.i above, following
notification from the line manager and/or HR, Local or
EMEA IT shall arrange for access to Company
Networks to be revoked on the appropriate date.
e. Return of Company Devices
i. All employees must return BCER-owned devices to
their line manager upon termination of employment
with the Company.

3. Screen lock
a. Technology permitting, local or EMEA IT shall install and 
maintain a time activated automatic lockdown function ("Screen 
Lock") on all BCER-owned Devices with access to Company 
Networks. The purpose of the Screen Lock is to reduce the risk 
of unauthorized access to Networks and Information Assets 
should a Device be lost, misplaced, left unattended, or stolen.
b. The Screen Lock will activate upon a reasonable period of nonuse of the Device, as determined by the Senior Manager of local
or EMEA IT, in consultation with senior business leaders. Once
activated the Screen Lock will lock out access to the Device until
the user inputs the correct Password. From time-to-time local or
EMEA IT will establish and communicate appropriate security
protocols to address excessive attempts by a person to enter an
incorrect Password.
c. Employees and other persons with access to Company Networks
shall install Screen Lock on any personal Devices used to access
Company Networks.
4. Physical Security of Certain Information Assets
a. All persons with access to Company Networks shall be required
to comply with security standards for locations and facilities that
store, process or maintain IT Systems and Networks as
established and communicated by local or EMEA IT from time to
time.
5. Additional requirements for Mobile Devices.
a. Mobile Devices used to access Company Networks or 
Information Assets, whether personally owned or BCER-owned, 
must meet the following requirements and specifications:
i. Support remote wipe capability;
ii. Support over the air (OTA) configuration by local or
EMEA IT or Company-authorised personnel, including
password reset, device configuration, remote locking,
and application installation/removal;
iii. Allow for installation of, and run, local or EMEA ITprovided management agents and/or configurations 
when connected to BCER systems or data as 
appropriate.
iv. May not be jail-broken, rooted, or similar state where
the underlying Operating System or bios has been
compromised;
v. Running a BCER supported operating systems or bios; 
and
vi. Support encryption of data transmission and storage.
b. Before disposing or transferring ownership of a Mobile Device 
all BCER data must be removed.

Support encryption of data transmission and storage.
b. Before disposing or transferring ownership of a Mobile Device 
all BCER data must be removed. BCER may require a full or 
partial Device wipe at its discretion.

c. BCER will enforce full device wipe after a set number of failed 
login/unlock attempts.
d. Non BCER-owned or -controlled data may be wiped, erased, or 
otherwise accessed by BCER in the course of securing or 
managing the Mobile Device.
e. Only BCER-approved Applications may be installed on 
BCER-owned Mobile Devices. Local or EMEA IT will 
implement controls to enforce this requirement.
f. Mobile Devices, whether personally- or BCER-owned, may be 
subject to legal holds or discovery.
g. Location services may be used with appropriate oversight to
locate device Mobile Device.
h. Local or EMEA IT will establish and communicate documented
processes and controls enforcing these requirements.
B. Employee Security Requirements 
1. Anyone with access to BCER Information Assets, Networks, or Devices
is expected to take reasonable measures to safeguard and protect 
them against unauthorized access, including but not limited to the 
following: 
a. Mobile Devices left in the office overnight should be physically
secured at the end of each workday either by removing them or
locking them in a secure place (file cabinet, drawer, etc.).
b. While traveling personal possession of Devices should be
maintained at all times unless prohibited by law or the
transport company.
c. In accordance with Section IV.A.2.c above, sharing
o
f Network or Device Passwords or other personal
user identification is prohibited.
d. The Screen Lock function on all Devices should be activated
when leaving a workstation unattended during regular working
hours and at the close of business.
e. Unauthorized access or use of Confidential Information,
or a lost or stolen Device, Password or Information Asset,
should be reported immediately to the appropriate
supervisor and local or EMEA IT.
C. Confidential Information Assets 
1. Reproduction or Distribution
a. Confidential Information may only be reproduced or
distributed in accordance with applicable policy,
agreements, laws, or regulations.
b. Notwithstanding the above, reproduction or distribution
of private or personal information such as employment
records, health records, etc., requires approval of the
Head of HR department.

of private or personal information such as employment
records, health records, etc., requires approval of the
Head of HR department.
2. Encryption of Confidential Information
a. Global IT will develop and adopt encryption standards and
protocols for the handling and transfer of Confidential

Information in compliance with the minimum requirements of 
the most stringent applicable laws or regulations. 
3. Disposal of Confidential Information
a. Disposal of Confidential Information may be accomplished
through the shredding of paper media, erasure of magnetic
data, or by delivery to a bonded salvage company, which will
provide a written Certificate of Destruction or comparable
document. Client or vendor data must be disposed of in
accordance with the terms and requirements of applicable
contractual agreements.
D. Software Copyright and Intellectual Property 
1. Third-party Software and Intellectual Property
a. BCER prohibits illegal, unauthorized or unlicensed use of
third-party software or other intellectual property on any
Company Networks, or Devices used for BCER work activities. 
All employees are required to act in compliance with the terms 
of BCER EMEA Third Party Software and Intellectual Property 
Policy.
2. BCER Proprietary Software and Intellectual Property
a. All Information Assets developed by, for, or on behalf of BCER
by any Company employee(s), contractor(s), vendor(s), or any
other source is:
i. Owned by, and intended for the exclusive use of,
BCER, and
ii. May not be used for any other purpose unless
expressly approved in writing by the Senior Manager
of the local or EMEA IT department.
3. Security Awareness Training
a. All employees must complete the annual awareness training
program as implemented by Global IT.
E. Audits and Global Standards 
1. Security controls will meet the minimum requirements of the most stringent
laws or regulations globally or nationally, as relevant.
2. On an annual basis EMEA or Global IT will audit the effectiveness of this
and other information technology and related measures designed to
protect Information Assets and Confidential Information.
a. Global IT will issue or update Global Required Minimum
Security Standards based on the annual assessment described in
the paragraph above. The Standards may contain non-material
differences depending on laws and local conditions in the
various global regions in which BCER maintains operation.
F. IT Disaster Recovery Requirements 
1. Roles and Responsibilities
a. Business Continuity Office. The Business Continuity Office is

responsible for ensuring that Business requirements for 
information technology resiliency are known and documented 
and for ensuring that significant risks associated with IT, 
Network, and IT Services recovery are managed and 
transparent. 
b. IT. Local or EMEA IT is responsible for creating, maintaining and
testing IT Disaster Recovery plans, providing regular information
on recovery risks and IT Disaster Recovery, and maintaining a
central database of Information Assets, which includes a list of
current Business Application Owners.
c. Business Applications Owners. Business Application Owners
are responsible for:
i. communicating business requirements to local or
EMEA IT and the Business Continuity Office, and
ensuring business support to complete IT Disaster
Recovery planning and testing, or acknowledging
acceptance of risk; and
ii. notifying local or EMEA IT and the Business Continuity
Office when an Application is no longer in use or the
usage profile will substantially change, e.g., The
amount of revenue generated will substantially
increase, or the user base will substantially increase, in
order to insure appropriate IT Disaster Recovery
planning.
G. Requirements 
1. The IT Department and the Business Continuity Office will jointly develop
standards to meet business and regulatory requirements for IT Disaster
Recovery. The standards will be updated or reviewed on an annual basis.
The standards will define the operational procedures to ensure that:
a. On a regular basis, the Business Continuity Office department
will request an assessment of the impact of a failure or outage
for Information Assets from Business Application Owners.
b. IT Department will develop and maintain plans and procedures
to ensure recovery capabilities meet business and regulatory
requirements as defined by Business Owners.
c. The IT Department will ensure that recovery risks and IT DR
status of designated information assets are reported to Business
Continuity Office on a regular basis.
The Business Continuity Office will assess recovery risks. Significant risks 
require tracking and Business Application Owner notification. Where no 
resolution is intended, an acceptance of the risk must be acknowledged by 
the Business Application Owner. 
H. Condition of Employment 
1. Compliance with this Policy is a condition of employment and/or continued 
affiliation with BCER.

Where no 
resolution is intended, an acceptance of the risk must be acknowledged by 
the Business Application Owner. 
H. Condition of Employment 
1. Compliance with this Policy is a condition of employment and/or continued 
affiliation with BCER. Any person or entity who violates the Policy, or 
attempts to subvert Company security, access controls, and/or other 
restrictions placed on the use of Networks or Devices shall be subject to 
discipline, up to and including termination.

Monitoring and Logging Policy

1 Introduction 
1.1 Background 
1.1.1 Monitoring and logging of BCER systems will be carried out in order to preserve the 
confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data held upon BCER information systems. 
1.2 Objectives 
1.2.1 On‐going system monitoring and logging for audit should allow timely detection of and response 
to unauthorized information processing activities. 
1.3 Scope 
1.3.1 The provisions of this policy apply to all BCER employees and contractor employees using or 
operating BCER Information Systems, as well as the systems and networks, and to contractor 
employees providing services to BCER by using BCER networks. 
1.4 Responsibilities 
1.4.1 Identifying responsibilities and or applicability, helps to ensure individuals or groups expected to 
follow a policy understand what their obligations are. 
1.4.2 All employees, contractors and temporary staff are required to comply with this Monitoring and 
Logging Policy and associated processes in relation. 
1.4.3 Monitoring and log analysis of BCER Information systems will only be undertaken by certain 
members of IT teams or by third parties explicitly appointed for this purpose, who will act under Non‐
Disclosure Agreements (NDAs). 
1.4.4 Information System owners are responsible for liaising with the appropriate IT team to get 
logging and monitoring set up for their systems. 
1.5 Support 
1.5.1 For further information and support, please contact the EMEA IT Compliance and Security team.

2 Monitoring Policy 
2.1 Networks, computers, internet usage and email usage may be monitored by members of the 
IT Team, or third parties contracted on behalf of BCER, and usage logged. 
 BCER networks, computers, internet usage and email usage is monitored and logged for all lawful 
purposes including: 
• Tracking the flow of network traffic
• Facilitating and improving capacity planning
• Maintaining good availability of network bandwidth
• Ensuring use of resources is authorised
• Management of systems
• Protecting against unauthorised access
• Ensuring system security
• Preventing and detecting crime
2.2 During monitoring, information may be examined, recorded, copied and used for authorised 
purposes. 
2.3 All information, including personal information, stored on or sent over BCER systems may 
be monitored. 
2.4 During the monitoring process, personal data may be inadvertently seen or accessed by staff 
authorised to perform monitoring . 
2.5 Monitoring will be automated in the detection and removal of viruses, malware, spam, 
pornography, inappropriate content and other activities which are in breach of the BCER acceptable 
use policy. 
3 Logging 
3.1 Logs are kept secure and will only be accessed by authorised members of IT. 
3.2 Critical logs will be centrally archived and secured remotely from the server where the activity 
occurred. 
3.3 Critical logs will be stored in a format that cannot be edited or modified 
3.4 Critical logs will be kept for 18 months. 
3.5 Audit logs for critical servers that record user and system activities, exceptions, and information 
security events shall be produced, and kept for an agreed‐upon time period, to assist in future 
investigations and access control monitoring. This will include recording, when relevant and within 
the capacity of the logging system, all key events. Key event data will include: 
• date/time for the event, and the event type;

• user‐ID and/or system‐ID associated;
• terminal identity and/or location;
• network addresses and protocols;
• records of successful and unsuccessful system accesses or other resource accesses;
• changes to system configurations;
• use of privileges;
3.6 System administrator and system operator activities shall be appropriately logged, as part of the 
general audit trail process. 
Governance 
3.1 Enforcement 
3.1.1 This policy is effective immediately. 
3.1.2 All authorised users of BCER information systems and data must comply with and adhere to 
this policy. Failure to do so could lead to appropriate sanctions against an individual or 
organisation. 
3.3 Document Review 
3.3.1 This document will be reviewed annually. 
3.4 Management Approval 
3.4.1 This document is reviewed approved, signed annually and issued on a version control basis.
